claims.text: Greg Short asserts that entrepreneurs who divide their attention across multiple businesses are destined to lose perpetually against focused competitors in 2026, because diversifying mindshare prevents the depth of competitive investment required to win in any single domain.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Competing in a market with focused single-business operators
Ambition to have the most successful business year
claims.mechanism: Mindshare is finite; spreading it across multiple businesses reduces the concentration of effort and competitive intensity required to beat focused operators in any individual domain.

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that focusing on one thing every single day materially increases the probability of winning, and that this single-focus discipline was the causal mechanism behind growing a business from a home attic start to multi-hundred-million-dollar scale over approximately a decade.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.mechanism: Sustained single-domain focus compounds competitive depth over time; Greg Short and his wife grew their business to multi-hundred-million-dollar scale specifically by maintaining monotonous focus on one thing throughout the company's ~decade-long history.
bounded_by: Speaker does not specify which industries or market types the single-focus rule applies to

claims.text: Greg Short argues that owning or running multiple businesses only sounds impressive but yields no actual competitive advantage; the appearance of success (sounding sexy) is the only output of multi-business diversification.
claims.speaker: Greg Short

examples.text: Greg Short and his wife built a multi-hundred-million-dollar business starting from her father's attic approximately a decade before 2026. Short attributes the company's scale directly to maintaining monotonous focus on one thing throughout the entire period, using this origin story as a first-person proof point for the claim that single-domain focus is the primary driver of outsized business outcomes.

practices.text: Focus on one business or one domain every single day rather than splitting attention across multiple ventures.
